## `lighthouse`

```text
Usage: lighthouse [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...

  lighthouse-cli – CLI for D2L Brightspace LMS at lighthouse.manipal.edu.

  Read course data and manage local downloads through the D2L REST API. Run
  'lighthouse auth login' first to set up your session. Commands with
  ``--json`` emit one command-specific JSON value on stdout; the option is
  per-command and diagnostics go to stderr. ``submit`` and instructor creation
  commands write remotely. ``download`` and ``sync`` write local files and
  manifests across a course or semester scope.

Options:
  --version  Show the version and exit.
  --help     Show this message and exit.

Commands:
  announcements  Show announcements.
  assignments    Show dropbox folders (assignments) for a course.
  auth           Manage authentication (session cookies).
  calendar       Show calendar events.
  config         Manage configuration (course tracking, semester mapping).
  content        Show content tree for a course (modules > submodules >...
  courses        List all courses.
  download       LOCAL WRITE: download files from a course or semester...
  grades         Show grades.
  instructor     Instructor assessment workflows and submission records.
  quiz           Show detailed info for a specific quiz.
  quizzes        Show quizzes.
  semesters      List all semesters.
  student        Student assessment workflows and submission records.
  submit         REMOTE WRITE: submit a file to a D2L dropbox folder.
  sync           LOCAL WRITE: incrementally sync new or changed files.
```

### `lighthouse assignments`

```text
Usage: lighthouse assignments [OPTIONS] [COURSE_ID]

  Show dropbox folders (assignments) for a course.

  Lists all assignment dropbox folders with name, due date, and attachment
  count. Use COURSE_ID to show assignments for a specific course, or omit to
  show assignments for all enrolled courses (parallel fetch).

  Output:   - Human: table with ID, Name, Due Date, Attachments columns   -
  JSON:  structured with folder details, attachments list,            custom
  instructions, and availability info

Options:
  --json  Output this command's JSON result.
  --help  Show this message and exit.
```

#### `lighthouse auth login`

```text
Usage: lighthouse auth login [OPTIONS]

  Log in to D2L through Microsoft SSO.

  Credentials come from --user, LIGHTHOUSE_USERNAME/PASSWORD, encrypted saved
  credentials, or interactive prompts. Passwords are never accepted as
  command-line arguments because process metadata can expose them.

  In an interactive terminal, the plain command is the normal path:

    lighthouse auth login

  Enter your email and password, choose from the verification methods
  Microsoft reports for your account, then enter the fresh code or approve the
  request. The command saves and verifies the session before showing useful
  next steps.

  MFA flags remain available for scripts and explicit selection: auto, sms,
  call, app, push, or choose. Text codes may arrive via SMS or WhatsApp
  depending on Microsoft; the CLI cannot select the delivery channel. Voice
  calls are approved by answering and pressing #; push is approved in
  Microsoft Authenticator.

  Discover what the account supports first: lighthouse auth mfa-methods

  Session cookies typically expire after ~5 days (MAHE tenant policy); re-run
  login when auth status fails. --save-credentials stores email/password only.

  Non-interactive SMS/WhatsApp recovery uses two commands so the fresh code
  stays tied to the same Microsoft challenge. First run lighthouse auth login
  --mfa-method sms. Then run lighthouse auth verify <code>.

  Do not run login twice — each login sends a new code. In a TTY, login alone
  prompts for the code after it is sent.

  On success, D2L session cookies are saved to ~/.config/lighthouse-
  cli/cookies.json.

  Use --save-credentials to store email/password encrypted (requires: pip
  install lighthouse-cli[credentials]). You still re-authenticate when cookies
  expire.

Options:
  --user TEXT                     Username (email) for Microsoft SSO.
  --totp TEXT                     Authenticator app code, or '-' to enter a
                                  fresh text code after it is sent.
  --mfa-method [auto|sms|app|call|push|choose]
                                  MFA: sms, call, app, push, choose, or auto.
                                  A plain interactive login shows the methods
                                  Microsoft reports for your account.
  --save-credentials              Save email/password encrypted for future
                                  logins (session cookies still expire ~5
                                  days).
  --json                          Output this command's JSON result.
  --help                          Show this message and exit.
```

#### `lighthouse auth mfa-methods`

```text
Usage: lighthouse auth mfa-methods [OPTIONS]

  List the account's MFA methods without triggering a challenge.

  Performs a real sign-in through the post-password stage and may advance
  KMSI/session state, but stops before BeginAuth. Reports OneWaySMS (sms),
  TwoWayVoice* (call), PhoneAppOTP (app), and PhoneAppNotification (push).

Options:
  --user TEXT  Username (email) for Microsoft SSO.
  --json       Output this command's JSON result.
  --help       Show this message and exit.
```

```text
Usage: lighthouse auth refresh [OPTIONS]

  Refresh cookies from a signed-in browser through loopback CDP.

  The browser must already be running with a CDP port and signed in to
  lighthouse.manipal.edu. Use ``auth login`` for the pure-HTTP SSO flow.

Options:

                   LIGHTHOUSE_CDP_PORT or 34165).
  --json           Output this command's JSON result.
  --help           Show this message and exit.
```

#### `lighthouse auth verify`

```text
Usage: lighthouse auth verify [OPTIONS] CODE

  Complete login with the verification code from the current ``auth login``
  session.

  Use after ``auth login`` prints "Verification code sent." Do not run a
  second ``auth login`` — that sends a new code and invalidates the previous
  one.

Options:
  --json  Output this command's JSON result.
  --help  Show this message and exit.
```

#### `lighthouse config courses`

```text
Usage: lighthouse config courses [OPTIONS]

  Manage course tracking and semester mapping.

  Without flags, runs interactive setup: shows all enrolled courses and lets
  you pick which to track and assign semester labels. ``--reset`` clears this
  local mapping only. It does not delete downloads or alter courses in the
  LMS. Use ``--json`` for this command's list/result.

  Examples:
    lighthouse config courses                    # Interactive setup
    lighthouse config courses --list             # Show tracked courses
    lighthouse config courses --add 44347 -s "Sem IV"  # Track one course
    lighthouse config courses --remove 44347     # Stop tracking a course
    lighthouse config courses --reset            # Clear all tracking

Options:
  --add TEXT           Track a course by ID or name.
  --remove TEXT        Stop tracking a course by ID.
  -s, --semester TEXT  Semester label to assign (used with --add).
  --list               Show tracked courses.
  --reset              Clear local course tracking only; keep downloads and
                       LMS data.
  --json               Output this command's JSON result.
  --help               Show this message and exit.
```

### `lighthouse download`

```text
Usage: lighthouse download [OPTIONS] [COURSE_ID]

  LOCAL WRITE: download files from a course or semester scope.

  If COURSE_ID is given, download that course. Without COURSE_ID, downloads
  the latest configured semester. Without trustworthy course configuration,
  the command fails closed before writing local files.

  This command writes local files and a manifest under --output-dir. It does
  not change anything in the LMS. --dry-run prints the plan without writing.
  --force replaces local manifest metadata and fetches every file.

  Scope options:   --semester  Filter the omitted-COURSE_ID scope to a
  semester (by name or ID)   --also      Add additional course(s) to that
  omitted-COURSE_ID scope

  Assignment options:   --include-assignments  Download attachments from all
  dropbox folders   --assignment           Download a specific dropbox folder
  --attachment           Download a specific attachment (requires
  --assignment)

Options:
  -o, --output-dir TEXT       Custom download directory.
  --dry-run                   Preview downloads without changing disk.
  --json                      Output this command's JSON result.
  --force                     Replace local manifest metadata and re-download
                              every file.
  --types TEXT                Comma-separated content types to download
                              (file,html). Default: file.
  -s, --semester TEXT         Filter to a specific semester (requires tracking
                              config).
  --also TEXT                 Additional course(s) to include by name or ID.
  --include-assignments       Also download assignment attachments.
  --assignment INTEGER RANGE  Download a specific assignment folder's
                              attachment(s).  [x>=1]
  --attachment INTEGER RANGE  Download a specific attachment from an
                              assignment folder.  [x>=1]
  --help                      Show this message and exit.
```

```text
Usage: lighthouse instructor quiz-create [OPTIONS] COURSE_ID

  Create a hidden quiz shell, with no questions or gradebook link.

  Add questions through Brightspace; the public quiz API supports reading
  question definitions but not creating them. one-way means one question per
  page and no backward navigation. all means all questions together.

  --name TEXT               [required]
  --layout [all|one-way]    [default: all]
  --attempts INTEGER RANGE  [default: 1; 1<=x<=10]
  --yes
  --dry-run
  --json
  --help                    Show this message and exit.
```

### `lighthouse submit`

```text
Usage: lighthouse submit [OPTIONS] COURSE_ID FOLDER_ID

  REMOTE WRITE: submit a file to a D2L dropbox folder.

  COURSE_ID is the course identifier (numeric OrgUnitId or name substring).
  FOLDER_ID is the dropbox folder identifier (numeric folder ID or name
  substring).

  Use `lighthouse assignments COURSE_ID` to discover available folders with
  their IDs.

  Example:   lighthouse submit "signals" "Assignment 1" --file solution.pdf
  lighthouse submit signals "Assignment 1" --file solution.pdf --yes

  This command changes remote LMS state. The command prompts for confirmation
  before submitting (course name, folder name, file path). Use --yes to skip
  the prompt (required for agent/automation use).

  On success, prints a JSON object with submission_id, folder_id, folder_name,
  course_id, course_name, file info, and submitted_at timestamp.

Options:
  -f, --file TEXT  Path to the file to submit.  [required]
  --yes            Skip confirmation prompt and submit immediately.
  --json           Output this command's JSON result.
  --help           Show this message and exit.
```

### `lighthouse sync`

```text
Usage: lighthouse sync [OPTIONS] [COURSE_ID]

  LOCAL WRITE: incrementally sync new or changed files.

  Uses .lighthouse.json manifest to skip unchanged topics. Without COURSE_ID,
  syncs the latest configured semester. Without trustworthy course
  configuration, the command fails closed before writing local files.

  This command writes local files and manifests. It does not change anything
  in the LMS. --force replaces local manifest metadata and fetches every file.
  Use --json for this command's structured result.

  Scope options:   --semester  Filter the omitted-COURSE_ID scope to a
  semester (by name or ID)   --also      Add additional course(s) to that
  omitted-COURSE_ID scope

Options:
  -o, --output-dir TEXT  Custom download directory.
  --json                 Output this command's JSON result.
  --force                Replace local manifest metadata and re-download every
                         file.
  --types TEXT           Comma-separated content types to sync (file,html).
                         Default: file.
  -s, --semester TEXT    Filter to a specific semester (requires tracking
                         config).
  --also TEXT            Additional course(s) to include by name or ID.
```
